0.0.n: This time expression needs no particle here.

0.1.n: This is the brand name of a robot vacuum cleaner.

0.2.n: Marks ルンバ as what the speaker sets up; the verb comes in the next line.

1.0.n: Japanese nouns do not distinguish singular and plural; here the context indicates children.

1.1.n: Marks 子供 as the ones who leave.

1.2.n: The plain form describes the departure used as a time reference for 前.

1.3.n: Gives the amount of time before the children leave.

1.4.n: With 出る10分, it places something ten minutes earlier than departure.

1.5.n: Makes the ten-minute interval approximate rather than exact.

1.6.n: Marks the approximate time chosen for the Roomba to start.

1.7.n: 設定する becomes 設定している for an ongoing setting, then 設定していて to connect to what follows.

2.0.n: This brand name refers to the same robot vacuum mentioned earlier.

2.1.n: Marks ルンバ as the thing that starts moving.

2.2.n: 動く changes to 動き before 出す, which adds the sense of beginning an action.

2.3.n: Links the Roomba starting to the regular response it triggers.

3.1.n: This interjection signals a sudden realization.

3.3.n: Suggests the children notice that departure time has arrived.

3.4.n: The destination particle に or へ is omitted in this casual speech.

3.5.n: The plain form modifies 時間, telling us what it is time to do.

3.6.n: 行く時間 means the time for going, rather than the duration of a trip.

3.7.n: Connects the noun 時間 to explanatory ん; it is not a separate adjective ending here.

3.8.n: Short for の in んだ, which presents the statement as an explanation or realization.

3.9.n: The plain ending completes なんだ, giving the realization a casual tone.

3.11.n: Casual form of という, linking the quoted realization to こと.

3.12.n: Turns the quoted thought into something that can be understood.

3.13.n: Marks the whole quoted idea as what is understood in the next line.

4.0.n: Refers to the children who recognize that it is time to leave.

4.1.n: Marks the children, though に would be more standard with 分かってもらえる; this sounds like a spoken blend.

4.2.n: 分かる in て-form plus もらえる expresses being able to receive someone’s understanding as a benefit.

4.3.n: Introduces a reason and leaves the following consequence unstated in this excerpt.

0.tip: を points forward to 設定していて in the next line, so this is not a complete sentence.

1.lit: Having it set for about ten minutes before the kids leave…
1.tip: 出る10分前 means ten minutes before leaving; ぐらい makes that timing approximate.

2.tip: A verb stem plus 出す means to begin doing that action.

3.lit: The fact that, “Oh, it’s already time to go to school”…
3.tip: っていうことを packages the quoted realization as the object of understanding in the next line.

4.lit: Because I can get the kids to understand…
4.tip: The intended meaning is clear, but 子供に分かってもらえる would be the more standard wording.
